newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs down on data in thin range.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs down on data in thin range.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures came under slight pressure from an unexpected rise in Japan's machinery orders for October.
But dealers said volumes were thin and trade was confined to narrow ranges as interest dwindled ahead of the year end.
"The selling brought it down two to three ticks. That's hardly enough to put a trade on," said a European bank dealer.
September Euroyen was quoted at 99.18 at 1115 GMT after falling to a low of 99.16 against its IMM close at 99.20. March JGBs settled at 125.67 against their previous 125.82.
"The general feeling is that yen rates can't move down much more and the futures are getting expensive. But it's the year end and the market's awash with liquidity," said the trader.
He said players would be increasingly sidelined for the rest of the month unless the dollar broke above 115 yen or below 110 yen, or Japanese economic data showed unexpected strength.

Eurodollar futures finished mildly firmer as players continued to buy them back after Friday's sell-off on the back of comments by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan, which triggered renewed fears of a rate hike.

"I think the bias is for the Eurodollars to trade a bit higher. We probably won't see a Fed tightening. If anything, there could be an easing further down the road," said the trader, adding that recent U.S. economic figures provided no signs of inflationary pressures.
March Eurodollars ended at 94.50 against its IMM close at 94.48. June finished at 94.40 against 94.38.
